deep.reconstruction:
This is the opening of an axiomatic definition of a 'tame' (modéré) structure on R. For each n ≥ 1 there is a family M_n of subsets of R^n. Every map u:[1,n]→[1,m] of finite sets induces a coordinate map u*:R^m→R^n, (x_j) ↦ (x_{u(i)}). The previous page states four axioms:
- M1: direct images u*(A) of sets in M_m lie in M_n. This covers coordinate projections, permutations and diagonal embeddings.
- M2: for u surjective (so u* is a diagonal-type embedding), preimages u*^{-1}(B) lie in M_m.
- M3: A ∩ u*^{-1}(B) lies in M_m.
- M4: products, A×B in M_{m+n}.

This page first sums up the reduction to generators. Every map of nonempty finite sets factors through permutations, elementary degeneracies and elementary faces, as in the simplicial category. So, keeping M4, the axioms M1–M3 can be replaced by:
- (a) stability under permutations of coordinates.
- (b1)/(b2) stability under the image and the preimage of the elementary diagonal embedding α_n*: R^n → R^{n+1}, (x_1..x_n) ↦ (x_1..x_n,x_n).
- (c1) A ∩ β_n*^{-1}(B) ∈ M_{n+1}, where β_n* is the projection forgetting the last coordinate.
- (c2) the projection β_n*(A) ∈ M_n.

In logical terms, the M_n are closed under substitution, equality (diagonals), conjunction and existential quantification. These are the positive-primitive ('regular') operations, with no complements, unions or ambient spaces R^n required. Intersection is derived on the previous page as A∩B = Δ^{-1}(A×B).

Section ③ then sets aside degenerate cases.
- By M1, if one M_n is empty, all are, since some map [1,n]→[1,m] always exists. This trivial case is excluded by assuming (*) M_1 ≠ ∅.
- If some M_n contains ∅, all do, since u*(∅)=∅. If none does, each M_n is nonempty, stable under binary intersection and avoids ∅, hence a filter base on R^n. This case is excluded by assuming (**) ∅ ∈ M_1, hence ∅ ∈ M_n for all n.
- The NB, continued on the next page, observes that adjoining ∅ (M'_n = M_n ∪ {∅}) preserves the axioms, so (**) costs no generality.

The overall aim is a framework for 'topologie modérée': which systems of subsets of R^n can serve as the tame sets. This is the programme later announced in Esquisse d'un programme and realised in the literature as o-minimal structures.
errors: The reduction of general M3 to c1 is not spelled out. It does hold: for iterated projections, use A ∩ β^{-1}(β'^{-1}(B) ∩ β(A)) = A ∩ β^{-1}β'^{-1}(B), via c1 and c2. For diagonal-type u*, use M2 plus stability under intersection, which needs M4. So M4 must indeed be kept alongside a)–c), as the text implicitly does.
The statement 'si un des M_n est vide, tous le sont' needs n,m ≥ 1 so that maps [1,n]→[1,m] exist. This is fine since n ∈ N*.
Small slip: '∅ ∈ M_n ∀ n ∈ N' should read N*.

ideas.what: Indexing definable-set families by finite sets, with all coordinate maps u* induced by maps of finite sets acting by image and preimage.
ideas.modern_name: FinSet-indexed structure / hyperdoctrine-style presentation of a first-order structure (Lawvere theory viewpoint)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lawvere (hyperdoctrines, ca. 1969); van den Dries (structures on R as sequences S_n, 1980s)
ideas.where_published: Only the general idea of tame topology appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), without this axiomatics

ideas.what: Reduction of the axioms to generators: permutations, elementary diagonal (degeneracy) and elementary projection (face).
ideas.modern_name: Generators of FinSet / the simplicial category; elementary definability operations

ideas.what: Positive axiom system: closure under images by projections, preimages by diagonals, intersections and products, with no complements or unions.
ideas.modern_name: Closure under primitive-positive (regular) definitions; relational clones / co-clones (minus the constant relations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Geiger 1968; Bodnarchuk–Kaluzhnin–Kotov–Romov 1969 (relational clones); regular logic in categorical logic

ideas.what: Excluding degenerate cases: all M_n empty; M_n without ∅, which are then filter bases; adjoining ∅ preserves the axioms.

missed.claim: Grothendieck's starting axioms for tame sets form exactly the 'regular' / primitive-positive fragment. This is closure under substitution along coordinate maps, equality, conjunction and existential projection, without negation. It coincides with the closure conditions defining relational clones in universal algebra. O-minimality instead starts from Boolean algebras of sets with the full first-order closure. Here a filter-base degenerate case is even identified, which the o-minimal literature never isolates. The positive-first presentation, building complements in later if at all, links tame topology to pp-definability, Pol–Inv Galois theory and regular categories. That link does not seem to be made in the o-minimality literature.
missed.quote: chaque M_n (étant stable par intersection de deux ens.) est une base de filtre sur R^n
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests studying 'positive tame structures' and their Boolean or o-minimal completions, as regular versus coherent theories. It also suggests reading tameness through the lens of CSP/relational-clone theory over R.

missed.claim: This is a dated (1973–1978 or later) axiomatisation of structures on R via coordinate maps of finite sets. It predates van den Dries's 1984 formulation of structures as sequences of subsets of R^n stable under projections. It documents Grothendieck's independent route to the o-minimal framework.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is history-of-mathematics priority: an independent, earlier, categorical formulation of what became o-minimal structures.

deep.surprise_reason: That Grothendieck sketched an axiomatics of tame topology is known in outline from the Esquisse. The concrete content here is new detail but mostly routine: a FinSet-indexed, purely positive (pp-closure) axiom system with degenerate-case analysis, apparently predating van den Dries. It is mildly notable as an independent, positive-logic route to o-minimality.

This page: '(d'où ∅∈M_n ∀n∈N)': the manuscript has N (probably intended N*).
The last line 'dans presque[?]' is more likely 'alors en posant' (or similar), leading into the next page's 'M'_n = M_n ∪ {∅}'.
In a), the struck-out text precedes '∀n∈N*, σ∈𝔖_n, A∈M_n, on a σ*(A)∈M_n'; the reading is correct.
